sentences.text: Navigators use ordinary-sounding words with exact meanings, and the exam will happily swap one for another to see if you notice.
Heading is the direction your bow is pointing at this instant.
It wanders as the boat yaws.
Course is the direction you intend to steer.
Track, which your GPS calls course over ground, is the direction the boat actually moves over the bottom.
So when would heading and track be different?
Whenever wind or current is pushing you sideways.
You’re pointed one way and sliding another.
Speed over ground is how fast you’re really covering the bottom, as opposed to your speed through the water.
And a bearing is the direction from your boat to an object.
It can be true, magnetic, compass, or relative.
